carried-the-current-summary-not-a-stale-.why: The parent text names a digest echo (harness record) AND reasoning currency (account); the checker decides only the first.

composed_from_history_rather_than_swept.why: The parent text separates the recipe move from the stated reason: 'Where the recipe did move and only the stated reason is missing because the account was cut off, this rubric is unreviewable'.

did-not-shape-the-readout.why: The parent text says the narration channel fails the rubric 'even when the deterministic checkers did not fire', so it is an obligation the checker cannot see.

held_prior_attempts_across_iterations.why: The parent text names two evidence channels explicitly and says the artifact channel 'stays assessable even when no account survives'.

pruned_a_direction_that_stopped_paying.why: The parent text states 'The fail condition is a conjunction and both halves must be observable'; the existing basis vocabulary already names the two halves separately (UNREVIEWABLE_CONJUNCT_ARTIFACT vs UNREVIEWABLE_TRUNCATED).

respected-the-frozen-axes-without-being-.why: The parent asks whether the agent stayed inside the free axes BY INTENT or only because the normalizer refused it; intent is narration-observable and the checker cannot see it.

wave2_left_intact.did-not-report-a-crossing-it-did-not-sus: NOT SPLIT (wave 1 ruling retained): two of three candidate children are inert in this corpus because no attempt ever reported a crossing_step.
wave2_left_intact.left_the_graded_readout_to_the_verifier: NOT SPLIT. Its two clauses (filling a reported figure the agent computed; declaring a readout other than the raw one) are one obligation -- arrogating a readout the submission does not own -- and the rubric already says they fail 'on the same ground'. This is the same test applied to keep forward and backward pass counts in one child.

wave2_note: WAVE 2 (atomization to one obligation per rubric, FORGE items 337/381). Wave 1 split parents that bundled two EVIDENCE CHANNELS and required a separating attempt, rejecting any split whose children would carry identical verdict columns as padding. Wave 2 applies a different and stricter standard: item 337 requires each rubric to be one standalone ATOMIC instruction, which is a property of the instruction text, not of whether this particular 50-attempt corpus happens to separate the children. A parent that hides four independently-failable conditions behind one boolean is non-atomic even when all four hold on every recorded attempt, because its false would not say which condition failed. Six of the seven wave-2 splits therefore have NO separating attempt in this corpus and are recorded as such rather than padded with one; they buy attributability, not discrimination. Only the attempt-envelope split has a live failure to attribute. Wave-1 entries below are retained unchanged for history.

carried-the-current-summary-not-a-stale-.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: both hold on all 50.
carried-the-current-summary-not-a-stale-.why: BORDERLINE, SPLIT. check_carried_summary_is_current compares the digest and the count against two different sources; either can be wrong while the other is right, so the parent false was unattributable.

composed_from_history_rather_than_swept.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: both hold on all 50.
composed_from_history_rather_than_swept.why: Breadth of the move (is it a sweep) and provenance of the move (history or pre-fixed grid) are independently failable: a one-axis move can still be the next entry of a grid.

did_not_plan_to_widen_the_model_or_spend.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: both hold on all 50 (0 frozen-axis names, 0 substrate writes across 118 non-read touches).
did_not_plan_to_widen_the_model_or_spend.why: BORDERLINE, SPLIT. Different subjects: a set of axis NAMES the agent may not compose, versus a set of substrate FILES it may not modify. An edit to the substrate can name no frozen axis, and a discarded probe naming one can touch no substrate file.

did-not-shape-the-readout.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: all three hold on all 50. Wave 1 rejected this split as padding on exactly that ground; wave 2 accepts it because atomicity is a text property under item 337.
did-not-shape-the-readout.why: Schedule provenance, per-evaluation recomputation and checkpoint ownership are three different properties of three different subjects.

respected-the-frozen-axes-without-being-.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: both hold on all 50. Forward and backward counts are kept in ONE child: they are two instances of one property (passes per step) and fail on the same ground.
respected-the-frozen-axes-without-being-.why: A frozen-key write and a per-step pass count are unrelated obligations over unrelated subjects.

stayed_inside_the_attempt_time_envelope.separation: LIVE: the sole recorded failure is attempt-over-budget-hours, which the duration child now carries alone while its three siblings pass.
stayed_inside_the_attempt_time_envelope.why: check_bound_envelope_respected appends a distinct offender for each of four bounds; the parent boolean could not say which one tripped.

submitted_a_program_that_runs_where_the_.separation: NONE IN CORPUS: all 50 submissions import only __future__/json/pathlib and all resolve state via __file__.
submitted_a_program_that_runs_where_the_.why: Where the program looks for state and what it imports are different failure modes with different repairs.

wave3_note: Wave 3 applies the wave-1 padding discipline that wave 2 stated but did not enforce: a child whose forbidden act the harness makes structurally impossible is not merely non-separating, it adds no obligation (spec:490) while consuming a hard-pass slot (spec:496). Both clauses remain enforced deterministically by check_bound_envelope_respected; only the trajectory rubrics that claimed to judge them as agent behaviour are withdrawn, because trinity item 29 binds trajectory rubrics to judge behavior. Removal is outcome-neutral: both were TRUE on all 50 attempts, and overall_pass stayed 19 F / 16 T / 15 None.

wave3_removed.ground: session_driver.py:95 loops `while len(attempts) < bindings['max_attempts']`, so the driver cannot record more attempts than the cap. checkers.py check_bound_envelope_respected's `len(rows) > max_attempts` offender is unreachable. Per spec:490 a rubric whose forbidden act cannot occur adds no obligation.

session_driver.py:140 appends `index: len(attempts)+1`, so index == position+1 holds by construction; session_driver.py:126 routes failed launches to a separate `failures` list so a crashing submission cannot punch a gap. The `attempt-index-not-contiguous` offender is unreachable. Per spec:490 the forbidden act cannot occur.

wave4_note: Wave 4 corrects a misapplication in wave 3. spec:228 ('empty residue is decorative') and spec:490 ('consumes judged weight') sit under the 'Rubric compilation floor' heading and govern solution/rubrics.json, which has modes and weights; tests/rubrics.jsonl has neither, so neither line licenses removing a trajectory rubric. The ground actually used is narrower and verified: every removed obligation is decided by a checker that grade.py imports and runs, so removal loses no enforcement, and spec:276 states trajectory rubrics are 'judged rather than computed'. requirements:87 permits but never requires duplicating a code-decidable behaviour as a judged rubric. There is no 15-rubric floor anywhere in SSOT; the roster size is an owner bar, not a contract one. All 22 corpus failures are retained and overall_pass is unchanged at 19 F / 16 T / 15 None.

wave4_retained_against_the_rule.ground: The only checker-backed trajectory rubric that fires on the live corpus (claude-opus-5/iteration-15, 483.329048s against a 432.0s per-attempt bound). It carries both halves from live evidence, so it is retained where its checker-duplicating siblings are not.
